source.title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds

accepted.question_text: The paper introduces two notions of deformation for connected complex manifolds in the noncompact setting. One is a C-infinity map f: X -> Y whose fibers are connected complex n-manifolds given by local fiberwise complex coordinates, without assuming properness or C-infinity local triviality. The other is a holomorphic surjective submersion π: X~ -> D over a complex disc with central fiber X that is locally trivial in the C-infinity category. Under what hypotheses are these two notions equivalent, or when does one imply the other?

evidence.quote: Remark 7. Note that in Def. 3 we are not assuming that f is locally trivial in the C∞-category. Def. 3 is not the same that [GR, Def. 9].
Question 1. Under what conditions we can say that the two notions of deformations mentioned above are equivalent, or one implies the other?

accepted.question_text: How should one compare the notion of cobordism with the notion of deformation for compact complex manifolds?

evidence.quote: Question 2. Compare the notions of cobordism and deformations of compact manifolds.

accepted.question_text: How should one compare deformations of complex manifolds with boundary with families of cobordisms?

evidence.quote: Question 3. Compare the notion of deformations of manifolds with boundaries with the notion of families of cobordisms.

accepted.question_text: Let n >= 2. If an n-dimensional complex manifold M with boundary admits nontrivial deformations, what kind of cobordism must exist between the connected components of its boundary ∂M?

evidence.quote: Question 4. Let n ≥ 2. If an n-dimensional complex manifold M with boundary has nontrivial deformations, then what type of cobordism exists between the components of ∂M?

accepted.question_text: Is there a numerical invariant for manifolds with boundary that detects rigidity, in the same way that Whitehead torsion detects when an h-cobordism is a cylinder?
accepted.context_brief: Rigidity invariant for manifolds with boundary

evidence.quote: Question 5. Is there a numerical invariant that characterizes when a manifold with boundary is rigid, similarly to the way Whitehead torsion characterizes when an h-cobordism is a cylinder?

accepted.question_text: Can the definitions and basic properties of deformations of manifolds with boundary be reformulated naturally in the language of groupoids and torsors?

evidence.quote: Question 6. Express the definitions and properties of deformations of manifolds with boundaries in the language of groupoids and torsors.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex space and let X' be a compactification of X with boundary D = X' \ X. Under what conditions does every deformation of X arise from a deformation of the compactification X' together with a deformation of the analytic boundary set D?

evidence.quote: Question 7. Let X′ be a compactification of the complex space X. When are deformations of X obtained from deformations of X′ and deformations of the analytic set D := X′ \ X?

accepted.question_text: For the noncompact threefolds W_k = Tot(O_P1(-k) ⊕ O_P1(k - 2)), which deformations are compactifiable?

evidence.quote: Question 8. Determine which deformations of Wk are compactifiable.

accepted.question_text: For the noncompact threefolds W_k = Tot(O_P1(-k) ⊕ O_P1(k - 2)), describe all deformations that are projectivizable.

evidence.quote: Question 9. Describe all projectivizable deformations of Wk.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist nontrivial deformations of W_1 = Tot(O_P1(-1) ⊕ O_P1(-1)), despite the fact that W_1 is formally rigid?

evidence.quote: Question 10. Decide whether there exist nontrivial deformations of W1. Note that [GKRS] proved that W1 is formally rigid.

accepted.question_text: Consider a compactifiable or projectivizable deformation (Xcal, D, Y, f, o, j) of X = W_k, where W_k = Tot(O_P1(-k) ⊕ O_P1(k - 2)). For which parameters t in Y does the fiber f^{-1}(t) admit a surjection to P1 extending the structure of X ∩ f^{-1}(t) as an affine bundle over P1? For which t is the fiber f^{-1}(t) at least covered by projective subspaces of codimension 1?
accepted.context_brief: Affine-bundle structures in deformations of W_k

evidence.quote: Question 11. Consider a compactifiable (or projectivizable) deformation (X , D, Y, f, o, j) of X = Wk. For which t ∈ Y is there a surjection f^{-1}(t) −→ P1 extending the structure of X ∩ f^{-1}(t) as an affine bundle over P1? For which t ∈ Y is f^{-1}(t) at least covered by codimension 1 projective spaces?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a compactifiable complex space X for which no nontrivial deformation of X is itself compactifiable?
accepted.context_brief: Spaces with only noncompactifiable nontrivial deformations

evidence.quote: Question 12. Does there exist a compactifiable space X such that no nontrivial deformation of X is compactifiable?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a toric Calabi-Yau threefold. What geometric conditions on X force all deformations of X to be compactifiable, if any such conditions exist?
accepted.context_brief: Compactifiability criteria for toric Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.quote: Question 13. Let X be a toric Calabi–Yau threefold. Determine what conditions on X imply that all of its deformations are compactifiable (if any).

accepted.question_text: Let X be a pseudoconcave complex space. When does there exist a compact complex space W and an open embedding j: X -> W such that the complement W \ j(X) is very small, for example a finite set?

evidence.quote: Question 14. Let X be a pseudoconcave complex space. When is there a compact complex space W and an open embedding j : X −→ W such that W \ j(X) is “very small”, for instance a finite set?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex space. Construct a completion Xbar containing X as an open subspace, for example a compact topological space in which prescribed sequences, or even all sequences, of points of X have convergent subsequences landing in Xbar. Then endow Xbar with a complex-space structure, and classify those complex spaces X for which the boundary Xbar \ X is small, such as a finite set.
accepted.context_brief: General completion program for complex spaces

evidence.quote: Question 15. Let X be a complex space. Find an object, say a compact topological space, X containing X with X open in X and for which certain sequences (or all sequences) of points of X have a subsequence converging to a point of X, then give a structure of complex space to X. Classify those complex spaces X such that X \ X is small, e.g. it is a finite set.

accepted.question_text: Solve the completion problem from Question 15 for pseudoconcave complex manifolds X satisfying Proposition 40. Concretely, X should satisfy one of the following source-stated hypotheses: either dim X = n >= 3 and for every x in X there exists t > 0 and sections f1, ..., ft of the t-th tensor power of the canonical bundle ω_X that give local coordinates at x; or, for every x in X there exists t > 0 and sections f1, ..., fn of ω_X^⊗t giving local coordinates at x and, for every distinct x,y in X, some section of a tensor power of ω_X vanishes at x but not at y.

evidence.quote: Proposition 40. Let X be an n-dimensional pseudoconcave complex manifold. Assume that one of the following conditions is satisfied: (1) either n ≥ 3 and for each x ∈ X there exists an integer t > 0 and f1, . . . , ft ∈ ω⊗t_X giving local coordinates at x; or (2) for each x ∈ X there exists an integer t > 0 and f1, . . . , fn ∈ ω⊗t_X giving local coordinates of X at x and for all x, y ∈ X such that x ≠ y there exists m > 0 and f ∈ H0(ω⊗m_X) such that f(x) = 0 and f(y) ≠ 0.
Question 16. Solve question 15 for spaces X satisfying the properties in Proposition 40.

accepted.question_text: Under what conditions does every deformation of the total space of a vector bundle again carry the structure of an affine bundle?

evidence.quote: Question 17. Under what conditions do all deformations of the total space of a vector bundle have the structure of affine bundles?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a noncompact Calabi-Yau threefold. What geometric conditions on X imply that X has infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic deformations?
accepted.context_brief: Infinite deformation families for noncompact Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.quote: Question 18. Let X be a noncompact Calabi–Yau threefold. What geometric conditions on X imply that it has infinitely many nonisomorphic deformations?

accepted.question_text: Let X be obtained from a complex manifold X~ by removing finitely many points. How do deformations of X compare with deformations of the compact or less punctured space X~?

evidence.quote: Question 19. Let X be obtained from X˜ by removing finitely many points. Compare deformations of X to those of X˜.

accepted.question_text: What cohomology theory correctly parametrizes deformations of noncompact complex manifolds, with the property that vanishing of this cohomology forces all deformations to be trivial?

evidence.quote: Question 20. What is the correct cohomology theory that parametrizes deformations of noncompact manifolds? (Vanishing of such a cohomology should imply existence of only trivial deformations.)
